headline: Phone recovered from suspect's house in Cumilla teen's murder investigation
summary: Police have recovered the phone of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim's mother from a suspect's house, a key development in the ongoing murder investigation. Three young men have been detained.
details: Police have recovered the phone belonging to the mother of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, who was found dead near Comilla University. The phone was found at the house of a suspect named Tuhin.

Inspector Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan, in-charge of Kotbari Police Outpost, confirmed this development to The Daily Star on Saturday night. Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is scheduled to brief the media today.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar. He was a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School.
Md Rakibul Hasan, OC of Cumilla Sadar South Police Station, previously stated that three young men, Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged 18-20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.
Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects. As of Saturday night, no case had been officially filed regarding the incident.
Opratim left his home around 3:00 PM on Friday, informing his parents that he intended to take photographs using his mother’s iPhone. He went missing shortly after.
His body was tragically discovered on Saturday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after his disappearance. It was found in the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of Cumilla.

headline: US to sell 60,000 2000-pound bombs to Israel, worth billions
summary: The Trump administration has approved the sale of these powerful weapons, considered among the most destructive in the US arsenal, to Israel, a deal worth billions of dollars.
details: The US Trump administration is preparing to sell a total of 60,000 highly destructive bombs, each weighing 2000 pounds, to Israel. This multi-billion dollar agreement is currently being finalized between the two countries.

According to US media reports, the Trump administration has already approved the sale of these weapons, considered among the most deadly and devastating in the US arsenal. The decision has also been informally communicated to the US Congress.
